title: window.open Promise(s)
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Chrome has gotten [some feedback](https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/partitioned-popins/issues/11) requesting a Promise-based interface for the `window.open` function, and we see two possible extensions that could assist:

1. Returning `Promise<WindowProxy>` instead of just `?WindowProxy` from some new naming for `window.open`, similar to what is discussed in [this thread](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7485). The promise would resolve either when the new window was initialized or the initial navigation completed and reject if the open failed or if no WindowProxy could be linked. This would be useful for the caller, as they could more easily wait for some more *ready* state to start interacting with the window without having to setup event listeners (which might depend on the opened window engaging with them).
2.  Adding a new function (e.g., `Promise<?object> waitForClose()`) on the `WindowProxy` when it's returned from a call to `window.open` and a new function (e.g., `void close(object)`) on the `window` object when a window was opened via `window.open`. The opener would await `waitForClose()` and see it resolved when the opened window was closed, if the close was done via `close(object)` then the object passed in by the opened window would be returned to the awaiting opener. This would be a more ergonomic API for a common pattern where one tab opens a new window for some sort of login or purchase action to complete, it could be accomplished now via `postMessage` but this would make the control flow cleaner.

I'm not sure if either of these changes yield enough benefit for it to be worth maintaining new versions of such old APIs, but they seemed worthy of discussion given similar ideas have come up a few times now.
